must_fix.issue: A stale `loopback_result_stash` entry gives a later question another call's results. This is a silent wrong value, and it reaches the native C ABI. If a question's redirect is absorbed before its `yourself` call is answered, the later answer is stashed under that answer id. Nothing removes the entry. The case is a cancelled question: `!question.cancelled` skips the hold. A deadline also cancels, and so does a yourself call still parked on a promise export. The C++ reference reuses the lowest free question id, so its next tail call with that id takes the stale frame. The question gets it at once, before the new call is even answered. The new call's own answer then goes stale in turn. This also happens on e9f37e1 (same probe, same output), so it is not a regression. But this item makes the stash the documented way that answer order does not matter, and it now stashes exception frames too, so a stale exception can fail a later tail call.

Id reuse: vendor/ext/capnproto/c++/src/capnp/rpc.c++:310 (`std::priority_queue<..., std::greater<Id>> freeIds`). Claims this breaks: CHANGELOG.md:56-57 ('When the named call is answered, the question gets the call's results, or its exception'), docs/native-abi.md:71-72.
must_fix.why: The C ABI delivers another call's value as this question's RETURN RESULTS, with no error. capnp_cancel or a question deadline while a C++ tail call is in flight is enough to set it up.

must_fix.suggested_fix: 1. Hold for cancelled questions too: drop `!question.cancelled` at mod.zig:6039. A late answer or Finish(Y) is then absorbed by the cancelled question, as it is today when the cancel comes after the redirect. 2. Drop `loopback_result_stash[id]` when an inbound Call arrives with that question id. A compliant remote reuses an id only after its Finish, and by rpc.capnp:484-492 that Finish comes after any redirect that names the id. 3. Do not stash the answer of a yourself call whose redirect was already used, for example one that was parked. Add the native probe as a regression test and ablate it.

must_fix.issue: The CHANGELOG says a failing `sendResultsTo = yourself` call is now answered with `resultsSentElsewhere`, and that 'this applies to sendReturnException'. That is false for yourself calls that fail or are parked before handler dispatch. The marker is recorded only in `dispatchImportedTargetPlan` (`.call_handler`) and `handleResolvedExportedCall`. These earlier failures still send an `exception` Return on the wire for the tail call: a rejected promise export (`.promise_broken`), an unknown capability, a failed `prepareParamCapsForDispatch`, and a queue or budget refusal. So does a call parked on our unresolved promise export that the host later rejects. All of them call sendReturnException with no marker yet. Also, a redirect that names a parked yourself call is not held: the question gets the bare tag at once. The native shim reports that as `unfollowed_tail_call_reason`, but native-abi.md says that reason is for a redirect that 'names no call with sendResultsTo = yourself'. All of this is the same on e9f37e1, so it is not a regression. The new claims are what is false.
must_fix.where: src/rpc/peer/call/peer_call_orchestration.zig:79 (`.promise_broken`, no note), :239 (unknown_capability returned before dispatch), :262 (parked with no marker); the marker is recorded only at :32 and :86. False claims: CHANGELOG.md:67-80 (headline, and 'This applies to sendReturnException and sendReturnExceptionTyped'); docs/native-abi.md:54 and :62-72 ('The question has no RETURN until then', 'The order does not matter').
must_fix.why: Wrong wire behaviour that the CHANGELOG says is fixed. The C++ reference rejects an exception Return for its tail call (rpc.c++:4055, 'Tail call `Return` must set `resultsSentElsewhere`, not `exception`') and drops the whole connection. This is reachable when a native host uses capnp_promise_export and C++ forwards parked calls back to it. A host that rejects that promise then kills the connection.

must_fix.suggested_fix: Either (a) record the yourself marker when the Call arrives, before routing or parking (third_party.noteCallSendResults at handleCall entry). Then every failure goes through completeSelfLoopbackException, and a redirect to a parked call is held. Pair this with must-fix 3: forwarded yourself calls would then hold, and they are answered through sendReturnTag. Or (b) narrow CHANGELOG.md:67-80 to calls that reach their handler. In that case, list parked and pre-dispatch yourself calls as a known limit in docs/native-abi.md, and fix the row-54 wording.

must_fix.issue: The documented fallback for non-settling answers never happens with a spec-following remote. CHANGELOG.md:38-45 and the field doc at mod.zig:764-769 say a held question whose call is answered another way 'waits for the remote's Finish of that call' and 'then ends with tail_call_finished_reason'. But rpc.capnp:489-492 has the tail caller send Finish for bar'() only after it receives Finish for bar(). The C++ reference keeps Y's QuestionRef in X's answer pipeline until Finish(X) (rpc.c++ handleFinish, `pipelineToRelease`). capnp-zig's own `.sent_elsewhere` forwarder relays Finish(Y) only on Finish(X) (`forwarded_tail_questions`). The held X sends no Finish, so it ends only at disconnect, a host cancel or a deadline. Before this change it ended at once with the bare tag. Also, 'HostPeer answers every call that way' is false: respondHostCallResults uses sendReturnResults (host_peer.zig:334). Only respondHostCallException and respondHostCallReturnFrame use the prebuilt path, and that path also puts a non-resultsSentElsewhere Return on the wire for a tail call.
must_fix.where: CHANGELOG.md:38-45; src/rpc/peer/mod.zig:764-769; the pin test 'a held tail call whose call is answered by a prebuilt frame waits for the remote's Finish' in tests/rpc/peer/rpc_reflected_direct_handler_test.zig. It injects Finish(Y) before Finish(X), an order no compliant remote sends.
must_fix.why: This is a false doc and CHANGELOG claim about the lens question 'is the hold always settled'. On these paths it is not settled until the connection ends, which is a liveness regression compared with the immediate bare tag. In practice, today's non-settling paths (HostPeer exceptions and prebuilt frames) also put a wrong Return on the wire for the tail call, and a C++ remote then drops the connection.
must_fix.suggested_fix: After a non-settling Return for a `yourself` call is sent, settle any hold with the bare redirect. Do it after the send, not inside clearSendResultsRouting, to avoid a callback in the middle of the send. Otherwise, correct the text: the question waits until the transport closes or the host cancels it, because a compliant remote sends Finish for the named call only after this question's Finish. Drop the 'every call' claim about HostPeer. Change the pin test to the spec order: Finish(Y) after Finish(X), never before.

nice_to_have: settleSelfLoopbackAnswer delivers to the held question in a defer, even when `sendReturnTag(.resultsSentElsewhere)` fails. By then completeSelfLoopbackReturn has removed the marker. docs/native-abi.md tells a host to answer a failed capnp_return_results with capnp_return_exception. On this path that sends a wire `exception` for the tail call (the marker is gone) after the question already got the results. Say in the docs that a send failure (as opposed to a build failure) must not be retried. Or keep the marker until the send succeeds.

A Finish(Y) that arrives during `build` (re-entrantly) settles the held question with tail_call_finished_reason. completeSelfLoopbackReturn then stashes the built frame anyway, which is another stale entry (see must-fix 1). Skip the stash when the marker is already gone after `build`.
handleFinish calls settleTailCallOnFinish after `try finish.handleFinishWithOps(...)` (mod.zig:4837-4845). An error there skips settling the hold. Settle first, or in a defer.

The new tests use only one wire order: Call Y, then the redirect, with Finish(Y) injected early. No test covers cancel before the redirect, a yourself call parked on a promise export, id reuse, or Finish(Y) after Finish(X). The probes above would close those gaps.

No conn_test or Peer test checks that Finish(X) goes on the wire after a held delivery. rpc.capnp:491 requires it, and the C++ reference waits for it before it sends Finish(Y). The Peer path does auto-finish, and native questions are retained and finished by the host. Assert this once.

Pre-existing, outside this item: a yourself call forwarded in `.propagate_results_sent_elsewhere` mode (a promise resolved to an import) never gets a redirect on the answering side. Its stash entry on the remote is stale from the start.

The C++ e2e_server resolve_disembargo run is still not done. Code reading suggests the main flow is covered: C++ RpcClient::call goes through directTailCall to the client's plain CallSequence export, so the marker is recorded at `.call_handler` before the redirect. A client that passes a promise export as `target` would hit must-fix 2.

must_fix.issue: A Return stashed for a `sendResultsTo = yourself` call can outlive that call. Nothing consumes it when its redirect never arrives. When the remote later reuses the question id, the stale Return goes to a later, unrelated question. da17e20 now stashes exceptions too (completeSelfLoopbackException -> settleSelfLoopbackAnswer), so a failed call's exception is misdelivered in a way it was not before. The cap-free results half is the same stash and is pre-existing (e9f37e1).
must_fix.where: Insert: src/rpc/peer/return/peer_return_send.zig:274-289 (settleSelfLoopbackAnswer), reached for exceptions from completeSelfLoopbackException at :237-252. Consume: src/rpc/peer/mod.zig:6034 takes the entry with no check that it belongs to the current call. Nothing drops the entry at Finish (by design, field doc at mod.zig:745-752). Nothing drops it when the id is reused either: noteSendResultsToYourself at src/rpc/peer/third_party/peer_third_party_routes.zig:524, and inboundAnswerQuestionIdInUse does not count the stash.
must_fix.why: An entry with no redirect to consume it appears whenever the question is cancelled or deadline-expired before the redirect arrives (a cancel that crosses the remote's tail call). mod.zig:6039 skips the hold for a cancelled question, so the redirect is absorbed. The host's later answer to Y, given before the remote's Finish(Y) arrives, then goes into the stash. The C++ reference reuses freed question ids lowest-first (vendor rpc.c++ ExportTable::next uses freeIds.top()), so its next tail call is likely to reuse Y. Call(Y') plus Return(X2, takeFromOtherQuestion=Y') then hits the stale entry. X2 gets the old call's results or exception at once, before the host has even seen the new call. The host's real answer is then stashed and goes stale in turn. This makes the CHANGELOG Fixed claim false ('the question gets the call's results, or its exception, as its one Return'). It also makes the docs/native-abi.md:71-72 claim false ('an answer that comes before the redirect is kept until the redirect arrives').
must_fix.repro: I ran this as a probe test in a scratch copy of src/native/conn_test.zig under testing.allocator. Steps: startTailCall; a.cancel(q); pushPendingTailCall(q, 77) (the redirect is absorbed); a.returnResults(77, 1111), or a.returnException(77, 'OLD call failed'); push Finish(77). The stash count is now 1. Then q2 = nextQuestion and pushPendingTailCall(q2, 77). q2 at once gets RETURN RESULTS 1111 (or EXCEPTION 'OLD call failed') before the host answers the new call 77. The host's answer 2222 is then stashed (stash count 1). On the e9f37e1 sources the results case does the same (pre-existing). The exception case stashes nothing there, and q2 gets 'unsupported Return variant', so the misdelivered exception is new in da17e20.
must_fix.suggested_fix: An entry is stale once a new call arrives under its id. The remote can reuse Y only after Finish(Y), and on the ordered connection every Return that names the old Y comes before that Finish. So drop the entry on reuse. In noteSendResultsToYourself (peer_third_party_routes.zig:524) add `if (self.loopback_result_stash.fetchRemove(answer_id)) |stale| self.allocator.free(stale.value);`. Doing this for every inbound Call id would be better. I checked this in the scratch copy: the probe then holds q2 and gives it 2222, and `mise exec -- zig build test-serialization test-rpc-peer` reports 147/147 steps and 1792/1798 tests passed (6 skipped). Add the probe as a conn_test case for both results and exception. If the fix waits, at least stop stashing exceptions and list the results half as a known limit.

nice_to_have: OOM after the mark is removed gives a wrong wire Return. settleSelfLoopbackAnswer already settles the call locally (held delivery in its defer, or the stash) before sendReturnTag(resultsSentElsewhere). If that send fails, sendReturnResults or sendReturnException returns an error and the native Conn keeps the answer pending (conn.zig:563-578). docs/native-abi.md:72-74 then tells the host to answer with capnp_return_exception. That answer goes on the wire as a plain exception (or results) Return for a tail call, which the C++ reference rejects as a protocol error, while the question has already had its RETURN. Native one-shot OOM sweep: answer_results k=9..13 gives X=results and Y on the wire=exception; answer_exception k=3..7 gives X=exception and Y=results; answer_first k=10..14 is the same. The Peer-level sweep shows the same at k=6..8. Exactly one RETURN per question and no leak held at every index of both sweeps. Possible fix: after a send failure that follows a settle, count the call as answered (a tombstone that drops the follow-up, or Conn removing the pending answer), or restore the mark so a retry sends resultsSentElsewhere again. The results path had the same gap before (e9f37e1 removed the mark before the build).

No committed test covers 'take the hold before the send' (peer_return_send.zig:265-268). I ablated it (look up before the send, take after it): every committed test stayed green. Only my probe failed: its Wire re-enters Finish(Y) inside the client's resultsSentElsewhere send, and the caller then got tail_call_finished_reason instead of its results. Commit that probe as a test. Also add a Peer.deinit-with-a-held-tail-call test. It passes today: one disconnected Return, no leak.

Pre-existing: completeSelfLoopbackReturn (peer_return_send.zig:196-205) has no errdefer effects.rollback(). If encodeReturnPayloadCapsWithEffects fails partway, the export refs of the entries already applied stay taken; sendReturnResults has the errdefer at :68. A 2-cap OOM sweep could not trigger it (refcounts stayed at 0), so it needs a larger cap table. Cheap fix: `defer effects.rollback();` before the encode.

CHANGELOG.md:40-45 says a held question answered through sendPrebuiltReturnFrame (HostPeer) 'waits for the remote's Finish of that call'. Neither reference remote sends Finish(Y) before our Finish(X). The Zig forwarder sends it only when Finish(X) arrives (peer_forward_orchestration.zig:143-162 and the tail Finish in handleFinish), and C++ drops Y together with X's answer. Both also reject the prebuilt `results` Return for a tail call: Zig with UnexpectedForwardedTailReturn (peer_forwarded_return_logic.zig:104-106), C++ at rpc.c++:4055. So in practice the question ends DISCONNECTED when the remote aborts, or hangs if a remote tolerates the frame. The pinned test sends Finish(Y) by hand. Say this in the CHANGELOG, or settle the hold with the bare redirect after sendPrebuiltReturnFrame's send.

Held delivery runs the question callback from inside sendReturnResults or sendReturnException, called by app or host code. If the callback fails, on_error runs there too, and ClientSession/ServerSession close the attached transport in it (client_wiring.zig:114). This happens without the enterJoinOperation guard that cancelQuestion takes for the same reason (peer_lifecycle.zig:556-564). The existing loopback-Return delivery path has the same gap. A guard, or a comment saying it is safe, would make the reentrancy contract explicit.

Minor: a stash entry for an absorbed redirect also stays until Peer.deinit (bounded by max_loopback_result_stash). The fix in must_fix removes it on id reuse but not otherwise. A note next to the stash field doc would help.
